nodes.content: Characterize bounds for dynamic treatment-regime effects under simultaneous unmeasured time-varying confounding and informative dropout.
requirements: Establish sharp identification bounds under explicit, separately interpretable confounding and dropout sensitivity constraints.
Construct confidence regions with at least 95% asymptotic coverage uniformly over the specified sensitivity class.

nodes.content: Optimize regime values over finite-history latent-response-type polytopes with separate confounding and dropout odds-ratio limits; project 95% multinomial confidence sets.
How can confounding and dropout odds-ratio limits handle zero-probability histories without sacrificing sharpness or uniform coverage?
Closed cross-product constraints and exact-binomial Bonferroni projection yield sharp bounds and at least 95% uniform coverage, including zero-probability histories.
Enumerate two-stage response types; encode separate zero-safe confounding and dropout constraints; prove sharpness and uniform 95% Bonferroni coverage.
Enumerate two-stage binary response types under separate zero-safe confounding and dropout constraints; assess 95% coverage in 10,000 structural-zero replicates.
TwoStageZeroSafe repository containing enumerated response types, constrained optimizers, and coverage summaries from 10,000 structural-zero replicates.
Audit TwoStageZeroSafe against exhaustive response-type bounds and estimate minimum 95% interval coverage across its 10,000 structural-zero replicates.
Across eight structural-zero scenarios, exhaustive bounds matched within 10⁻⁸; minimum empirical coverage was 96.1% over 10,000 replicates.
Use TwoStageZeroSafe to verify latent-law attainability at structural-zero optima and derive a finite-sample Bonferroni coverage proof.
A ninth structural-zero scenario exposed undefined 0/0 dropout odds: cross-product optimization returned an unattainable regime upper bound of 0.82.
What zero-cell dropout-odds semantics exclude the unattainable 0.82 bound while preserving sharpness and uniform 95% coverage?
Restricting dropout odds to positive-mass histories with positive denominators eliminates 0/0 optima without sacrificing sharpness or uniform 95% coverage.
Partition positive-mass histories by dropout-denominator support; optimize feasible latent laws and prove sharpness with uniform 95% Bonferroni coverage.
Reoptimize eight validated scenarios and the 0.82 counterexample using support partitions; test bound attainability and 95% coverage.
Eight scenarios retained their bounds; the ninth upper bound fell from 0.82 to attainable 0.76; minimum empirical coverage was 95.7%.
Using TwoStageZeroSafe, audit support-stratum boundary attainability and prove finite-sample 95% Bonferroni coverage for projected regime-value regions.
A positive-mass, all-dropout history violated denominator positivity; excluding its valid latent laws reduced 95% coverage to 91.3% across 10,000 replicates.
Explicit zero-retention strata retain all-dropout histories, exclude unsupported 0/0 completions, and yield sharp bounds with uniform 95% coverage.
Enumerate zero-retention strata, constrain positive-denominator odds, recheck the 0.82 and 91.3% counterexamples, then prove sharpness and uniform 95% coverage.
Reoptimize the ninth scenario with explicit zero-retention strata; test attainability and coverage against the prior 0.76 bound and 91.3% coverage.
Explicit zero-retention strata yielded an attainable 0.79 upper bound, versus 0.76, and raised empirical coverage from 91.3% to 95.8%.
Optimize support-stratified full-data transport couplings under separate confounding and dropout odds constraints; invert exact multinomial tests for regime effects.
Do pairwise transport constraints admit globally consistent three-stage latent laws, including zero-retention histories?
Pairwise transport constraints can admit incompatible three-stage marginals; a shared latent coupling eliminates spurious bounds, including at zero-retention histories.
Enumerate three-stage binary laws; compare pairwise/shared bounds and exact-test coverage across zero-retention strata at confounding ΓC=2, dropout ΓD=3.
At ΓC=2, ΓD=3, pairwise bound 0.86 was unattainable; shared-coupling bound 0.81 was attainable, with 95.6% empirical coverage.
Bound latent treatment and retention propensity deviations separately via total variation; optimize compatible full-data laws and invert exact multinomial tests.
Specify separate treatment and dropout total-variation budgets; enumerate compatible full-data laws, certify sharp extrema, and invert 95% exact multinomial tests.
Implement TV-Regime v0.1 for two-stage binary laws with treatment TV≤0.10 and dropout TV≤0.15; audit extrema and exact-test coverage.
TV-Regime v0.1 repository with full-data law enumerator, separate 0.10/0.15 TV constraints, extrema certificates, and exact-test inversion scripts.
Audit TV-Regime v0.1 extrema against exhaustive laws and exact-test coverage across 10,000 structural-zero replicates at TV budgets 0.10/0.15.
In 2,140 structural-zero replicates, absent-treatment histories lacked retention-propensity baselines, leaving dropout TV constraints undefined and sharp bounds uncertifiable.
Extend TV-Regime v0.1 with joint-mass dropout TV constraints for absent-treatment histories; compare sharpness certificates and exact-test coverage against conditional TV.
Joint-mass TV certified all 2,140 previously undefined cases; extrema matched within 10⁻⁸ and 10,000-replicate coverage reached 95.4%.
Does dropout joint-mass TV≤0.15 permit unrestricted informative dropout within histories occurring with probability below 0.15?
For a history with probability 0.08, joint-mass dropout TV≤0.15 permits complete conditional dropout deviation when other histories contribute zero.
Reanalyze the 2,140 absent-treatment cases with undefined retention baselines using certified joint-mass TV; test unrestricted dropout deviation at 0.08-mass histories.
At history mass 0.08, joint-mass TV≤0.15 admitted conditional dropout TV=1; worst-case regime-effect bounds widened by 0.08.
Use support-stratified additive-bias caps for treatment and dropout, optimizing shared full-data laws and projecting exact multinomial confidence sets.
How can additive dropout-bias caps handle all-dropout histories when retained outcome means are undefined?
Cap dropout outcome-mean differences only when both retention strata occur; leave all-dropout outcomes unrestricted for sharp, uniformly valid inference.
Partition retention supports, impose conditional mean-difference caps where defined, optimize shared latent laws, and prove sharpness plus uniform 95% coverage.
Enumerate two-stage binary laws with treatment bias≤0.10 and dropout bias≤0.15; audit all-dropout bound attainability and 10,000-replicate coverage.
Unrestricted all-dropout laws attained 0.76 with 95.5% coverage; support-stratified additive-cap projection excluded them, yielding 0.70 and 92.4% coverage.
Use support-stratified, history-normalized joint-mass selection caps for treatment and dropout; optimize shared latent laws and invert exact tests.
Formalize history-normalized treatment and dropout selection caps, enumerate zero-support latent laws, verify sharp extrema, and prove uniform 95% exact-test inversion.
Implement history-normalized joint-mass treatment/dropout caps (0.10/0.15); audit zero-support sharpness and 95% coverage in 10,000 replicates.
NormSelect v0.1 repository with history-normalized 0.10/0.15 selection caps, zero-support latent-law enumerator, sharpness certificates, and exact-test scripts.
Stress-test NormSelect v0.1 on all-dropout and 0.08-mass histories; certify attainable extrema and minimum coverage across 10,000 replicates.
At 0.08-mass histories, dropout remained constrained; all-dropout extrema matched exhaustive bounds within 10⁻⁸; minimum coverage was 95.3%.

Choose NormSelect: 0.79 zero-retention/0.81 shared-coupling findings demand safeguards; certification and 95.3% empirical coverage avoid undefined baselines, rare-history leakage, additive undercoverage.
